manifest.name: dsh-site-bridge
manifest.description: Chrome/Edge MV3 bridge for DeepSeek Harness: capture page markup (DOM, styles, selectors) and BFF traffic (xhr/fetch with headers and bodies) into a workspace snapshot bundle, drive the page with trusted CDP input, and verify injected scripts. Authorization never leaves the browser and is never written to disk.

scripts.test: node test/redact.test.mjs && node test/bridge.test.mjs && node test/artifacts.test.mjs && node test/plugin.test.mjs && node test/version.test.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh bundle patch: inserts the site-bridge row into a profile's layer stack.
# The bridge itself starts lazily on the first tool call (or immediately when
# `port` is set and `autoStart` is true).
- insert:
    - id: site-bridge
      name: 'dsh-site-bridge'

readme.text:
**English** · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Hands and eyes for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in your own browser.**
Capture a page's markup and its BFF traffic into files an agent can read, drive the page with trusted
input, and verify the extension you just wrote — live, in the same tab.

[](LICENSE)

Two halves, one bridge:

| Half | What it does |
|---|---|
| **DSH plugin** (`lib/`) | Owns the loopback bridge and exposes eleven tools to the model. Writes the snapshot bundle into the session workspace. |
| **MV3 extension** (`extension/`) | Lives in your Chrome/Edge profile, works with your cookies, captures markup and network over CDP, drives the page with real input events. Localized: English, Русский, 中文. |

Neither half is useful alone: the plugin holds the model-facing surface and the files, the extension
holds the browser session and the fidelity.

---

Writing an extension that embeds into someone else's site is mostly archaeology: what the markup is
actually made of, which selector survives the next deploy, and which BFF endpoint this button calls
with which payload. By hand that means DevTools, copy-paste and guesses.

This project turns the archaeology into a capture:

```
site_capture → captures/<host>/<timestamp>/
  dom.html          serialized markup of the captured scope
  dom.json          element tree: boxes, attributes, selector candidates
  styles.json       computed styles of key nodes + CSS custom properties

The agent reads those files like any other source and writes the extension. Then `site_inject` runs
that code in the live page, so "it should work" becomes "it works here".

- **Markup** — element tree with boxes and visibility, computed styles of interactive nodes, CSS
  variables of the theme, and selector candidates ranked by stability (`data-testid` > `id` > `name` >
  `aria-label` > class path > positional path), each checked for uniqueness against the live DOM.
- **BFF traffic** — `xhr`/`fetch` with method, status, request headers, request body, response
  headers and response body, scoped to the inspected site.
- **Trusted input** — clicks, typing, select, key presses, scrolling and file uploads through CDP
  `Input.*` / `DOM.setFileInputFiles`: events the page cannot tell apart from a human's.
- **Virtual cursor** — a DOM overlay that moves to the target plus a real mouse event at those
  coordinates, for controls that ignore synthetic `click()`.
- **Deep selectors** — `host >>> inner` resolves through open shadow roots and same-origin iframes;
  click coordinates are corrected for frame offsets.
- **Works in background tabs** — reading, clicking, typing and screenshots work while the tab is not
  focused (Chrome throttles only timers and animation there).
- **No stored credentials** — see [Security](#security).

readme.section: How this differs from browser automation plugins
readme.text:
There are plugins that hand an agent `browser_*` tools: navigate, click, type, read the page. This is
not one of them, even though it can do those things — input here is the instrument that verifies a
capture, not the product.

readme.section: How this differs from browser automation plugins
readme.text:
The product is the capture: the DOM with boxes and computed styles, theme CSS variables, selector
candidates checked for uniqueness, and the site's own xhr/fetch calls with headers and bodies, all
written to files an agent can read. Automation exists so that "this selector works" and "this BFF call
passes with my cookies" are checked against the live page instead of assumed.

readme.section: How this differs from browser automation plugins
readme.text:
The practical consequence: this plugin is built for writing an extension for one specific site, and
the input tools exist to verify that work against the live page rather than to browse the web.

- DeepSeek Harness with the `dsh` CLI and a profile (Desktop or Web).
- Chrome or Edge 125+ (the extension uses `chrome.debugger` and MV3 service workers).
- Node.js 22+ for the tooling in `tools/` and for the tests.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-site-bridge
```

That pulls the published package. From a local checkout instead:

```powershell

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1
```

The script links the plugin into your profile, adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles`, and stages the
extension into `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\site-bridge\extension`. Manual equivalent:
powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <path-to-this-repo>
```

Add `"dsh-site-bridge"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json`
if the CLI did not, then restart DSH — the host half loads at profile start.

1. `chrome://extensions` → enable **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** →
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\site-bridge\extension`.
2. Open the popup. It shows the port and the path to `bridge.json` (the same is printed by
   `site_status`).
3. Click **Import bridge.json** (`Импорт bridge.json` / `导入 bridge.json`) and pick that file, or
   paste the token — it saves itself, no button.
4. Open the page you want to work on and click **Connect this tab**.

Chrome shows the "started debugging this browser" banner: that is the CDP session everything runs
on. It disappears when you press **Disconnect**.

The popup UI follows the browser language: English, Russian and Simplified Chinese ship in
`extension/_locales`.

```text
site_status                     → bridge state, pairing path, tabs
site_tabs {action:"list"}       → tabs; claim/use/release/open/close/focus
site_network {action:"start"}   → begin recording, then act on the page
site_capture {screenshot:true}  → write the bundle into the workspace

A typical loop for writing a page-embedded extension:

1. `site_tabs` → bind the page.
2. `site_capture` → read `selectors.md`, `styles.json`, `api.md`.
3. Write the userscript / content script in your own repository.
4. `site_inject` with the script body → check that the anchor is found and the BFF call passes with
   the browser's cookies.
5. Iterate on the selectors the capture marked as fragile.

readme.section: Popup and tools are the same surface
readme.text:
The popup is a manual control for the person at the keyboard: attach a tab, detach it, start recording,
pick an element. The agent can do all of that through the tools, including `site_tabs {action:"claim"}`
for any tab it sees in `list`. The attach button is a human gesture, not a permission gate — the
bridge token is the only thing that decides who may drive the browser.

readme.section: Popup and tools are the same surface
readme.text: A pause button in the popup cuts the link from the browser side: the extension stops polling and refuses every command, so no tool can reach it or turn it back on. Only that button restores it, and the state survives a worker restart.

```
┌──────────────────────────── DSH host ────────────────────────────┐
│  tools (site_*)  ──►  bridge: 127.0.0.1, token, long-poll queue    │
│  redaction on ingest ──► in-memory buffer ──► artifacts writer     │
└───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘

The wire protocol is small and documented in [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md).

- **Credentials never leave the browser.** The extension does not read cookies or tokens: the page
  makes its own requests and the browser attaches them. The bridge sees them in flight, but values of
  `cookie`, `authorization`, `x-csrf-token`, `x-api-key`, `set-cookie` and similar headers,
  credential-shaped query parameters and credential-shaped JSON/form fields are replaced with
  `«redacted»` **on ingest** — before anything is stored.
- **Nothing credential-shaped is written to disk.** Header *names* are kept, because "this endpoint
  needs `x-csrf-token`" is part of the contract; the value is not.
- **Capture is site-scoped.** Only the inspected site's own `xhr`/`fetch` (same host, same
  registrable domain, or third-party JSON) is recorded. Telemetry and security agents that POST a full
  page dump to their servers are filtered out — otherwise page source with inline tokens would land in
  the bundle.
- **Loopback only.** The bridge binds `127.0.0.1` and rejects any request without the 32-byte pairing
  token. `site_status` prints the path to the token file, not the token.
- **Residual risk.** Header values and bodies still pass through the DSH process in memory. If a site

The bridge accepts only requests that carry the pairing token. The extension asks for `debugger`
instead of `<all_urls>` and does not inject a content script into every page. The cost is a pairing
step and Chrome's debugging banner. In exchange the permission is granted per tab, for the duration
of a session, and requests are read where they are made — no credential is copied out of the browser.

Attaching a tab is a decision for the person by default. The agent may list tabs freely, but
`site_tabs {action:"claim"}` on a tab the user has not attached is refused unless the call carries
`confirmed: true` — and the refusal names the tab, so the agent knows what to ask about. Closing a tab
the user attached needs the same confirmation. This is a rule inside the plugin, not an OS permission:
it makes the agent stop and ask instead of quietly widening what it can reach.

Cross-origin iframes, closed shadow roots and body size caps are analysed in
[docs/limitations.md](docs/limitations.md) — with the exact code location, the plan to remove each and
the expected cost.

```powershell
node test\redact.test.mjs     #  8 — redaction rules
node test\bridge.test.mjs     #  8 — wire protocol, token, liveness
node test\artifacts.test.mjs  #  5 — bundle layout and large-body spill
node test\plugin.test.mjs     #  2 — tool registration and the full tool path

`e2e.mjs` and `tools-chrome.mjs` launch a throwaway Chrome, load the extension with
`Extensions.loadUnpacked`, and exercise capture, trusted input, the virtual cursor, upload, injection
and screenshots against a local page with a working BFF endpoint.

```
lib/            DSH plugin: tools, bridge, redaction, artifact writer
extension/      MV3: service worker (CDP), popup, icons, locales
docs/           protocol, limitations, detailed guide
scripts/        install.ps1

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

The version lives in `package.json` and is mirrored into `extension/manifest.json`; `CHANGELOG.md`
holds the history. Every commit that changes shipped code bumps the version, docs-only commits do not:

```powershell
node tools\version.mjs check                  # fail if the three files disagree
node tools\version.mjs bump minor             # bump package.json + manifest.json + CHANGELOG stub
```

Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`. Versions below 0.3.0 were assigned retroactively from the commit
history, so an old tag may pin commit content that still carried the 0.1.0 stamp.
MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

[English](README.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · **中文**

**把 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的眼睛和双手放进你自己的浏览器。**
把页面的结构与其 BFF 流量抓取成智能体可读的文件，用可信输入驱动页面，并在同一个标签页里验证你刚写好的扩展。

[](LICENSE)

两部分，一座桥：

| 部分 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| **DSH 插件**（`lib/`） | 维护本机回环桥接，向模型提供八个工具，并把快照包写入会话工作区。 |
| **MV3 扩展**（`extension/`） | 运行在你的 Chrome/Edge 配置中，使用你的 Cookie，通过 CDP 抓取结构与网络，用真实输入事件驱动页面。已本地化：English、Русский、中文。 |

两者缺一不可：插件承载面向模型的接口与文件，扩展承载浏览器会话与保真度。

---

写一个嵌入别人网站的扩展，本质上是一场考古：页面结构到底是什么、哪个选择器能活过下次发版、这个按钮调用了哪个 BFF 接口、请求体长什么样。手工做这些就是 DevTools、复制粘贴和猜测。

这个项目把考古变成一次抓取：

```
site_capture → captures/<host>/<timestamp>/
  dom.html          被抓区域序列化后的结构
  dom.json          元素树：盒子、属性、选择器候选
  styles.json       关键节点的计算样式 + 主题 CSS 变量

智能体像读普通源码一样读这些文件，然后写扩展。接着 `site_inject` 把这段代码跑在活页面上，"应该能用" 就变成 "在这里能用"。

- **结构** —— 带盒子与可见性的元素树、交互节点的计算样式、主题 CSS 变量，以及按稳定性排序的选择器候选（`data-testid` > `id` > `name` > `aria-label` > class 路径 > 位置路径），每个都在活的 DOM 上检查过唯一性。
- **BFF 流量** —— `xhr`/`fetch` 的方法、状态、请求头、请求体、响应头、响应体，且只针对被检查的站点。
- **可信输入** —— 通过 CDP `Input.*` / `DOM.setFileInputFiles` 完成点击、输入、下拉、按键、滚动和文件上传：这些事件页面无法与真人操作区分。
- **虚拟光标** —— 一个移动到目标的 DOM 覆盖层，并在该坐标发出真实鼠标事件，用于忽略合成 `click()` 的控件。
- **深层选择器** —— `host >>> inner` 可以穿过开放的 shadow root 与同源 iframe；点击坐标会按 iframe 偏移校正。
- **后台标签页可用** —— 标签页不在前台时，读取、点击、输入和截图仍然可用（Chrome 只在后台限制定时器与动画）。
- **不保存任何凭据** —— 见[安全](#安全)。

readme.section: 与浏览器自动化插件的区别
readme.text:
有些插件给智能体提供 `browser_*` 工具：导航、点击、输入、读取页面。本项目不是其中之一，虽然这些都
能做——这里的输入是用来验证抓取结果的工具，而不是产品本身。

产品是抓取：带盒子与计算样式的 DOM、主题 CSS 变量、经过唯一性校验的选择器候选，以及站点自身的
xhr/fetch（含请求头与请求体），全部写成智能体可读的文件。自动化的作用是让「这个选择器可用」和
「这个 BFF 调用能带着我的 Cookie 通过」在活页面上被验证，而不是被假设。

实际后果：本项目是为编写面向某个具体网站的扩展而做的，输入工具用来在活页面上验证这些工作，而不是
用来浏览网页。

- 带 `dsh` CLI 与配置档（Desktop 或 Web）的 DeepSeek Harness。
- Chrome 或 Edge 125+（扩展依赖 `chrome.debugger` 与 MV3 service worker）。
- Node.js 22+，用于 `tools/` 里的工具和测试。

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-site-bridge
```

以上会安装已发布的 npm 包。从本地克隆安装则用：

```powershell

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1
```

脚本会把插件链接进你的配置档、写入 `dsh.profile.bundles`，并把扩展复制到 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\site-bridge\extension`。等价的手工步骤：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <本仓库路径>
```

如果 CLI 没写入，请把 `"dsh-site-bridge"` 加到 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 中，然后重启 DSH —— 宿主部分在配置档启动时加载。

1. `chrome://extensions` → 打开**开发者模式** → **加载已解压的扩展程序** → `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\site-bridge\extension`。
2. 打开扩展弹窗。它会显示端口和 `bridge.json` 的路径（`site_status` 也会打印同样内容）。
3. 点击 **导入 bridge.json**（Import bridge.json）并选择该文件，或直接粘贴令牌 —— 会自动保存，无需按钮。
4. 打开要操作的页面，点击 **连接此标签页**。

Chrome 会显示「已开始调试此浏览器」提示条：这正是全部功能所依赖的 CDP 会话。点击**断开**后消失。

弹窗界面跟随浏览器语言：英语、俄语、简体中文位于 `extension/_locales`。

```text
site_status                     → 网桥状态、配对路径、标签页
site_tabs {action:"list"}       → 标签页；claim/use/release/open/close/focus
site_network {action:"start"}   → 开始录制，然后在页面上操作
site_capture {screenshot:true}  → 把快照包写入工作区

编写页内扩展的典型循环：

1. `site_tabs` → 绑定页面。
2. `site_capture` → 阅读 `selectors.md`、`styles.json`、`api.md`。
3. 在你自己的仓库里写 userscript / content script。
4. 用 `site_inject` 注入脚本体 → 确认锚点能找到、BFF 调用能带着浏览器 Cookie 通过。
5. 针对快照标记为脆弱的选择器继续调整。

readme.section: 弹出窗口与工具是同一条通道
readme.text:
弹出窗口是给键盘前的人的双手控制：连接标签页、断开、开始录制、选择元素。智能体通过工具可以做同样
的事，包括对 `list` 中任意标签页执行 `site_tabs {action:"claim"}`。连接按钮是人的操作，而不是权限
闸门——能否驱动浏览器只由网桥令牌决定。

弹出窗口中的暂停按钮从浏览器一侧切断连接：扩展停止轮询并拒绝所有命令，任何工具都无法访问它，也无法恢复。只有该按钮可以恢复，且状态在 worker 重启后仍然保留。

- **凭据不离开浏览器。** 扩展不读取 Cookie 或令牌：页面自己发请求，浏览器自动附带。网桥能看到传输中的值，但 `cookie`、`authorization`、`x-csrf-token`、`x-api-key`、`set-cookie` 等请求头的值、形似凭据的查询参数与 JSON/表单字段，都会在**接收时**替换为 `«redacted»` —— 早于任何保存动作。
- **磁盘上不写任何凭据类内容。** 请求头的*名字*会保留，因为「这个接口需要 `x-csrf-token`」属于契约的一部分；值不会。
- **录制限定站点。** 只记录被检查站点自身的 `xhr`/`fetch`（同主机、同可注册域，或第三方 JSON）。把整页 HTML 转储到自己服务器的遥测与安全代理会被过滤掉 —— 否则含内联令牌的页面源码就会落进快照包。
- **仅回环。** 网桥只绑定 `127.0.0.1`，任何没有 32 字节配对令牌的请求都会被拒绝。`site_status` 打印的是令牌文件路径，而不是令牌本身。
- **残余风险。** 请求头与请求体仍会经过 DSH 进程的内存。如果站点把密钥放在非常规字段名下，脱敏无法识别。请像对待任何流量转储一样，把快照包视为敏感数据。

网桥只接受携带配对令牌的请求。扩展申请 `debugger` 而不是 `<all_urls>`，也不会向每个页面注入
content script。代价是配对步骤与 Chrome 的调试提示条。换来的是：权限按标签页、按会话授予，请求在
产生的地方被读取，凭据不离开浏览器。

默认情况下，连接标签页是人的决定。智能体可以自由列出标签页，但对用户未连接的标签页调用
`site_tabs {action:"claim"}` 会被拒绝，除非调用带有 `confirmed: true`——拒绝信息会指出具体标签页，便于
智能体询问。关闭用户自己连接的标签页同样需要确认。这是插件内部的规则，而不是操作系统权限：它让智能体
停下来询问，而不是悄悄扩大可达范围。
跨域 iframe、封闭的 shadow root 与响应体大小上限在 [docs/limitations.md](docs/limitations.md) 中逐条分析 —— 包含代码位置、消除方案与预估成本。

```powershell
node test\redact.test.mjs     #  8 —— 脱敏规则
node test\bridge.test.mjs     #  8 —— 协议、令牌、在线判定
node test\artifacts.test.mjs  #  5 —— 快照包布局与大体积响应体外置
node test\plugin.test.mjs     #  2 —— 工具注册与完整工具路径

`e2e.mjs` 与 `tools-chrome.mjs` 会启动一次性 Chrome，通过 `Extensions.loadUnpacked` 加载扩展，并针对带真实 BFF 接口的本地页面验证抓取、可信输入、虚拟光标、文件上传、注入与截图。

```
lib/            DSH 插件：工具、网桥、脱敏、快照包写入
extension/      MV3：service worker（CDP）、弹窗、图标、多语言
docs/           协议、限制、详细指南
scripts/        install.ps1

MIT —— 见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

版本号保存在 `package.json`，并同步到 `extension/manifest.json`；历史记录在 `CHANGELOG.md`。
任何改动发布代码的提交都要提升版本号，仅文档的提交不需要：

```powershell
node tools\version.mjs check                  # 三个文件不一致时报错
node tools\version.mjs bump minor             # 同步更新 package.json、manifest.json 与 CHANGELOG 条目
```

发布使用 `vX.Y.Z` 标签。0.3.0 之前的版本是按提交历史回溯标注的，因此旧标签指向的内容里
可能仍写着 0.1.0。
